newsitem.title: USA: U.S. plays down talk of formation of Group of Six.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plays down talk of formation of Group of Six.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers on Thursday sought to dampen expectations that his meeting next week with senior officials from five Asian economies was the prelude to forming a Group of Six.
"This is a meeting, not a group," he told reporters here.
The meeting, to be held March 4 in Tokyo, will bring together senior finance ministry and central bank officials from Australia, China, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore and the United States.
"In this meeting, we're bringing together representatives of a number of major outward-looking financial markets," Summers said.
"I'm looking forward to a useful discussion of a range of financial issues at a time when a great deal of financial change is underway in Asia," he added.
Topics to be discussed include banking and financial market regulation, developments in financial markets and the economic outlook.
Summers plans to hold bilateral talks with his Japanese counterparts while in Tokyo. He is also slated to visit Hong Kong for talks with officials there.
